task: Numerical ODE methods, nonlinear solvers, BVPs, and geometric integration source research
cache_policy: Copyrighted PDFs, extracted text, selected page renders, and the FNC checkout remain under the ignored scratchpad ODE source directory. Nothing was copied into active items or library pages.
method: I verified the actual cache files and hashes, then reread the proof ranges below. The failed worker reported complete reads of the named full chapters; this replacement role did not reread every page. sources.citation: Ernst Hairer and Gerhard Wanner, Introduction à l’Analyse Numérique, Chapter III: Équations Différentielles Ordinaires, University of Geneva course notes revised for 2004/05, June 2005; exercises in collaboration with Assyr Abdulle.
sources.license_and_access: Public author-hosted course-note PDF. No open license is asserted; cache remains ignored.
sources.prior_worker_checkpoint: Complete Chapter III, PDF pp. 1–30, as reported in the task handoff. This role did not independently reread the complete chapter.

independent_reading_ranges.sections: III.2–III.5: Runge–Kutta one-step error analysis, variable-step embedded estimates, and multistep definitions.
verified: One-step error proof separates a uniform local defect from step-map Lipschitz stability and propagates each local error.
Variable-step controllers use paired method outputs and an asymptotic error model; this is not a global accuracy theorem.
Multistep order is defined from the residual obtained by inserting exact solution values into the recurrence.

independent_reading_ranges.sections: III.6–III.8: multistep order, characteristic roots, and equal-step convergence.
verified: Root condition: all roots of rho are in the closed unit disk and unit-modulus roots are simple; repeated interior roots are allowed.
For equal steps, order p plus the root condition and O(h^p) starting values yields fixed-interval global O(h^p); proof uses a companion one-step system and propagated residuals.
The source restricts its proof to equally spaced steps.

independent_reading_ranges.sections: III.9: stiff test equations, A-stability and Runge–Kutta/multistep stability regions.
verified: A-stability means the test-equation region contains the closed left half-plane.
Explicit Euler has a bounded stability disk; implicit Euler is A-stable; BDF claims are tied to their root-locus conditions.
L-stability is not named in this source.

visual_checks.claim: Theorem 8.1 states the simple-unit-root condition and O(h^p) starter hypothesis.
A-stability definition and explicit/implicit Euler regions.

unread_parts.this_role_did_not_reread: The other pages of the chapter, including its geometric-integration section and exercises. Remaining chapters of the 168-page course-note collection were not used.

sources.license_and_access: Public author-hosted course-note PDF. No open license is asserted; cache remains ignored.
sources.prior_worker_checkpoint: Complete Chapter VI, PDF pp. 1–14, as reported in the task handoff. This role did not independently reread the complete chapter.

independent_reading_ranges.sections: VI.3 Newton method: Taylor error recurrence, local theorem, finite-difference Jacobian, frozen-Jacobian modification and damping.
verified: Local quadratic convergence assumes F is C^3, DF is invertible near the root, and the initial iterate is sufficiently close.
The source explicitly separates this local theorem from global convergence, which it says is poorly understood in general.
A frozen Jacobian generally loses quadratic convergence; damping is a practical modification.

unread_parts.this_role_did_not_reread: Fixed-point iteration, linear iterative methods, Gauss–Newton, and exercises outside PDF pp. 6–8.

sources.citation: Ernst Hairer, Geometric Numerical Integration, Lectures 1–3: Hamiltonian Systems, Symplectic Integrators, and Backward Error Analysis, TU München course notes, January–February 2010.
sources.license_and_access: Public author-hosted lecture PDFs. No open license is asserted; caches remain ignored.
sources.prior_worker_checkpoint: Complete lectures 1–3 (PDF lengths 14, 18, 20 pages) as reported in the task handoff. This role reread only the theorem/proof ranges listed here.

independent_reading_ranges.topic: Canonical two-form, symplectic maps, and Poincaré's Hamiltonian-flow theorem.
verified: The derivative of the flow satisfies the variational equation with symmetric Hessian; differentiating Phi_t'{}^T J Phi_t' gives zero, hence the flow is symplectic wherever defined.

independent_reading_ranges.topic: Symplectic Euler, Störmer–Verlet, and symplectic Runge–Kutta condition.
verified: Symplectic Euler has order one.
Störmer–Verlet composes two symplectic Euler methods and symmetry gives order two.
b_i a_ij + b_j a_ji = b_i b_j preserves quadratic first integrals and implies symplecticity.

independent_reading_ranges.topic: Formal modified equation, modified Hamiltonian, and finite-order near-energy theorem.
verified: The modified equation series is generally formal/divergent and must be truncated for rigorous estimates.
A symplectic method has a locally Hamiltonian modified equation; globality requires a domain condition or an explicit global assumption.
For smooth H, a symplectic method, globally defined modified Hamiltonian, and numerical orbit in compact K, Theorem 3 gives H^[N] drift O(t h^N), H error O(h^r), for t=nh<=C h^(−N+r).

visual_check.claim: Theorem 3 exact compact-orbit/global-modified-Hamiltonian hypotheses and energy estimates.

unread_parts.this_role_did_not_reread: Other pages in lectures 1–3. Lectures 4–5 and the cached introductory PDF were not used.

sources.prior_worker_checkpoint: Complete Markdown for chapters 4, 6, and 10, as reported in the task handoff. This role independently reread only the proof contracts listed below.

files_and_sections: newton.md: local quadratic-error derivation and its assumptions
newtonsys.md: multidimensional Newton update and convergence qualification
verified: The scalar quadratic-error derivation assumes the iterates already converge to a simple root; it is not a global convergence theorem.
The system chapter qualifies quadratic convergence as holding only under suitable conditions and when the iteration converges.

files_and_sections: euler.md: local truncation error and complete one-step error-recursion proof
zerostability.md: root condition/proof and Dahlquist equivalence
adaptive-rk.md: embedded estimates and step-size prediction
verified: The scalar one-step proof assumes uniform unit-LTE and derivative bounds, then iterates the geometric error recurrence.
The root-condition proof explicitly omits repeated roots; equivalence is stated but not proved in the chapter.
Adaptive control uses an asymptotic error guess and allows different local/global step exponents; it is not a certified global estimator.
Implicit steps require a root solve; the stiffness discussion is an example and operational motivation.

files_and_sections: linear.md: collocation, boundary rows, error identity, accuracy/stability
shooting.md: residual map and unstable example
nonlinear.md: nonlinear collocation residual and quasi-Newton implementation
verified: The linear BVP identity e=A^(−1)tau transfers truncation order only if the inverse norms are uniformly bounded; the source explicitly omits the stability proof.
Shooting reduces a BVP to a root problem through the IVP flow and has an unstable example.
Nonlinear collocation supplies an implementation and examples, not a general solver or mesh-convergence theorem.

unread_parts.this_role_did_not_reread: The remaining sections of these three chapter sources. Other chapters, exercise solutions, and repository material are outside the assigned evidence.

auxiliary_cache_orientation.use: Title page and table of contents only: confirmed course-note date, authors, printed chapter spans, and section map. No claims from other chapters are used.

source_limits: FNC's zero-stability proof omits repeated roots, and the Dahlquist equivalence theorem is stated without proof.
FNC Chapter 10 omits the uniform inverse-bound stability proof for BVPs.
Hairer Ch. III proves A-stability and discusses stiff stability regions but does not name L-stability.
The read sources use adaptive embedded differences as estimators and do not certify a global tolerance for the controller.
No read source supplies a general nonlinear BVP or shooting convergence theorem.
